# mongodb

MongoDB access patterns - bounded finds, filtered writes, aggregation pipelines; the model mongo adapter measures call sites against these.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-DATA-011` — MongoDB find/aggregate without a limit (medium)

An unbounded find or aggregation returns the whole result set into the application — memory and latency scale with the collection. The rule fires only when no limit()/batch_size() bounds the call.


Remediation: Pass limit= or chain .limit(n); paginate with a cursor or $skip/$limit in the pipeline.

Reference: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.limit/

### `AF-DATA-012` — MongoDB filtered write with an empty filter (critical)

delete_many({}), update_many({}, ...) or an empty Document() filter match every document in the collection — a mass write/delete from application code.


Remediation: Require a non-empty filter literal; gate legitimate mass operations behind an operational runbook.

Reference: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.deleteMany/
